```{r setup, include = FALSE}
has_deps <- requireNamespace("phyloseq", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("vegan", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  dpi = 120,
  eval = has_deps
)
```

This vignette covers the **statistical**, **machine-learning** and **genomics**
functions. Like the plotting family, the statistical and ML functions return a
`ggplot` by default and a tidy data frame (with the fitted model attached as an
attribute) when `return.data = TRUE`. For the figure functions see
`vignette("visualization", package = "micropubr")`.

```{r load}
library(micropubr)
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")
gp <- phyloseq::prune_taxa(
  phyloseq::taxa_sums(GlobalPatterns) > 5, GlobalPatterns)

# GlobalPatterns has no numeric covariates; add a few synthetic ones so the
# Mantel and variance-partitioning examples have something to chew on.
set.seed(1)
meta <- data.frame(phyloseq::sample_data(gp))
meta$pH    <- round(runif(nrow(meta), 5, 8), 1)
meta$Temp  <- round(runif(nrow(meta), 4, 37), 1)
meta$Depth <- round(runif(nrow(meta), 0, 100), 1)
phyloseq::sample_data(gp) <- phyloseq::sample_data(meta)
```

## Multivariate dispersion (PERMDISP)

`mp_dispersion()` tests whether group dispersions (spread around the centroid)
differ, the assumption behind PERMANOVA. Add ANOSIM/MRPP/PERMANOVA to the
caption with `add.test`.

```{r dispersion}
mp_dispersion(gp, group.by = "SampleType", add.test = "permanova")
```

## Mantel test

`mp_mantel()` correlates the community distance matrix with a distance built
from numeric metadata.

```{r mantel}
mp_mantel(gp, vars = c("pH", "Temp", "Depth"), method = "spearman")
```

## Variance partitioning

`mp_varpart()` partitions community variation among two or three explanatory
sets (each a vector of metadata columns).

```{r varpart, fig.height = 4}
mp_varpart(gp, groups = list(
  Chemistry = c("pH", "Temp"),
  Habitat   = "SampleType"))
```

## Prevalence and the core microbiome

`mp_prevalence()` draws a prevalence-abundance scatter (`"scatter"`) or a
core-microbiome heatmap across detection thresholds (`"core"`). The core taxa
are labelled automatically; pass `color.by` to colour points by a taxonomic
rank when it has only a handful of levels (colouring by `"Phylum"` here would
add a 60-entry legend, so we leave it off).

```{r prevalence, fig.width = 7.5}
mp_prevalence(gp, tax.level = "Phylum")
```

```{r prevalence-core, fig.height = 5}
mp_prevalence(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", plot.type = "core")
```

## Indicator species

`mp_indicator()` finds taxa significantly associated with groups (via
`indicspecies`). (Requires the `indicspecies` package.)

```{r indicator, eval = has_deps && requireNamespace("indicspecies", quietly = TRUE)}
mp_indicator(gp, group.by = "SampleType", tax.level = "Genus", top.n = 15)
```

## Differential abundance end to end

`mp_run_da()` runs a two-group test and returns a tidy table that
`mp_diff()` plots. The default `"wilcox"` method (Wilcoxon on centred
log-ratios) needs no extra packages.

```{r run-da, fig.height = 5}
da <- mp_run_da(gp, group.by = "SampleType",
                method = "wilcox", groups = c("Feces", "Soil"))
mp_diff(da, plot.type = "volcano", label.top = 8)
```

`"deseq2"`, `"aldex2"` and `"ancombc"` wrap the respective Bioconductor
packages when installed.

## Machine learning

`mp_ml()` trains a random forest (`"rf"`) or gradient-boosted trees (`"xgb"`)
on the feature table. The task is detected from the response: a categorical
`group.by` gives **classification**, a numeric one **regression**. (Requires
`randomForest` or `xgboost`, and `pROC` for ROC curves.)

```{r ml-import, fig.height = 5, eval = has_deps && requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly = TRUE)}
gp_genus <- phyloseq::tax_glom(gp, "Genus")
# Which genera discriminate sample types?
mp_ml(gp_genus, group.by = "SampleType", method = "rf",
      n.features = 15, seed = 1)
```

A two-class problem gives an ROC curve from out-of-fold predictions:

```{r ml-roc, fig.height = 5, eval = has_deps && all(vapply(c("randomForest", "pROC"), requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))}
two <- phyloseq::subset_samples(gp_genus, SampleType %in% c("Feces", "Soil"))
mp_ml(two, group.by = "SampleType", plot.type = "roc", seed = 1)
```

A numeric response switches to regression, scored by RMSE / R-squared:

```{r ml-reg, fig.height = 5, eval = has_deps && requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly = TRUE)}
mp_ml(gp_genus, group.by = "pH", method = "rf",
      plot.type = "prediction", seed = 1)
```

`return.data = TRUE` hands back the importance table with the fitted model,
cross-validation predictions and metrics attached as attributes:

```{r ml-data, eval = has_deps && requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly = TRUE)}
imp <- mp_ml(gp_genus, group.by = "SampleType", return.data = TRUE, seed = 1)
head(imp, 3)
attr(imp, "metrics")$caption
```

## Coverage plots

`mp_coverage()` draws sequencing depth across a genome from a data frame,
`samtools depth`, bedGraph/BED files, or a BAM (via `Rsamtools`).

```{r coverage}
set.seed(1)
cov <- data.frame(
  contig = rep(c("contig1", "contig2"), each = 100),
  position = rep(seq(1, 10000, length.out = 100), 2),
  depth = c(rpois(100, 60), rpois(100, 25)))
mp_coverage(cov, format = "data.frame")
```

## Circular genome plots

`mp_circos()` assembles an ideogram with optional coverage, GC, heatmap and
annotation tracks plus weighted ribbon links. (Requires `circlize`.)

```{r circos, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 6, eval = has_deps && requireNamespace("circlize", quietly = TRUE)}
genome <- data.frame(contig = c("c1", "c2", "c3"),
                     length = c(8000, 5000, 3000))
covc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genome$contig, function(ct) {
  L <- genome$length[genome$contig == ct]
  data.frame(contig = ct, position = seq(1, L, 50),
             value = runif(length(seq(1, L, 50)), 10, 90))
}))
links <- data.frame(contig1 = "c1", start1 = 500, end1 = 1500,
                    contig2 = "c2", start2 = 1000, end2 = 2000,
                    weight = 0.8)
mp_circos(genome, coverage = covc, links = links, link.by = "weight",
          coverage.type = "area")
```

## Chord diagrams

`mp_chord()` links the top taxa to the levels of a grouping variable, ribbon
width proportional to mean relative abundance. (Requires `circlize`.)

```{r chord, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 6, eval = has_deps && requireNamespace("circlize", quietly = TRUE)}
mp_chord(gp, group.by = "SampleType", tax.level = "Phylum", top.n = 10)
```
